notes.meaning: A wise son pays attention when his father trains and corrects him. A proud mocker, on the other hand, scoffs at anyone who tries to warn or rebuke him. Willingness to receive correction shows whether a person is truly growing in wisdom.

A person who speaks good and helpful words enjoys good things in return, finding inward peace and blessing. But people who are treacherous and unfaithful have an appetite only for violence and wrongdoing. In the end, what a person puts out with their lips comes back to feed their own life.

Keeping a close watch on what one says protects a person from harm and heartache. Blurting out whatever comes to mind without thinking invites sudden trouble and ruin. Learning to control the tongue saves a person from a world of regret.

A lazy person longs for plenty of good things but never gets them, because he refuses to do the hard work. In contrast, the person who works hard and stays faithful receives more than enough to satisfy his soul. Real fulfillment comes from steady effort rather than idle wishing.

A godly person genuinely hates lies, fraud, and dishonesty in every form. A wicked person acts deceitfully, bringing shame upon himself and disgust to others. Loving truth leads to lasting honor, while living a lie brings disgraceful exposure.

Living uprightly and honestly acts like an armor that keeps a person safe from ruin. Wickedness, however, trips up the sinner and brings about his downfall. God ensures that a clean heart leads to real security.

Some people pretend to be rich and put on a grand show, even though they have nothing of real value. Others pretend to be poor and live very simply, yet possess abundant wealth and spiritual riches. Outward appearances often hide the true condition of a person's life and soul.

A wealthy person can use his money to pay a ransom and buy his way out of danger when enemies attack him. A poor person never has to worry about kidnappers or extortion, because he has nothing they want to steal. Earthly riches bring heavy worries that the humble poor never have to carry.

The life and joy of a righteous person shine brightly and steadily like the sun. The prosperity of the wicked is like a small candle that flickers for a moment and is quickly blown out. Walking with God brings lasting gladness that outlives worldly success.

Pride is the root cause of arguments, fights, and broken relationships, because proud people refuse to back down. Those who are humble enough to ask for counsel and listen to good advice find wisdom and peace. Giving up stubborn pride quickly puts an end to bitter strife.

Money made quickly through gambling, fraud, or dishonesty soon disappears like vapor. But wealth gathered steadily by honest labor and patience grows and lasts over time. God blesses the steady work of our hands rather than dishonest shortcuts.

Waiting a long time for something you deeply want can make the heart weary, heavy, and sick. But when that longed-for blessing finally arrives, it brings fresh life, energy, and joy, like fruit from a tree of life. Trusting God in the waiting brings deep sweetness when His promise is fulfilled.

Anyone who looks down on God's word and ignores His commands brings destruction and debt upon himself. But the person who holds God's law in deep reverence and obeys it will be richly rewarded with peace and safety. Taking God's instructions to heart is the safest path in life.

The counsel of wise and godly teachers flows like a spring of fresh, living water that revives the soul. It gives people the insight they need to steer clear of deadly traps laid by sin. Listening to sound teaching keeps us safe on the road of life.

Good judgment and sound understanding win goodwill and respect from both God and people. But the path of unfaithful sinners is rough, rocky, and painful to travel. Doing what is right makes life far smoother than the hard road of rebellion.

A sensible person thinks carefully and acts only with clear facts and understanding. A foolish person rushes ahead, blabbing about things he does not understand and putting his foolishness on display for everyone to see. Thinking before acting keeps a person from public embarrassment.

An untrustworthy messenger who betrays his mission brings trouble on himself and ruins the business he was sent to do. A reliable, loyal ambassador delivers his message truthfully and brings healing, peace, and order. Faithfulness in carrying out responsibilities brings relief to everyone involved.

Whoever scorns instruction and refuses to be guided ends up in poverty and disgrace. But anyone who humbly listens when someone points out a mistake earns true respect and honor. Being willing to learn from correction opens the door to lasting success.

Reaching a good and godly goal brings deep, sweet satisfaction to the inner life. Yet fools refuse to enjoy true happiness because they detest letting go of their favorite sins. We cannot experience true satisfaction until we are willing to turn away from what is evil.

Spending time with wise, godly people rubs off on us and helps us become wise as well. But hanging out with foolish and reckless companions leads straight to moral ruin and destruction. Choosing our close friends wisely is one of the most important decisions we can make.

Trouble and disaster chase down persistent sinners like a hunter pursuing its prey. But God ensures that those who live uprightly receive a good reward for their faithfulness. Sin always brings its own painful payback, while righteousness leads to blessing.

A good person lives wisely and leaves a lasting legacy of faith, prayers, and honest goods that reaches even his grandchildren. Meanwhile, the riches collected by wicked people are eventually handed over into the care of the righteous. A life devoted to God builds an inheritance that endures for generations.

A poor farmer who works hard can produce plenty of food even from newly cleared ground. Yet that food can easily be wiped out through dishonesty, unfair treatment, or poor management. Hard work produces good fruit, but justice and careful stewardship are needed to keep it safe.

A parent who refuses to discipline a child does not truly love him, because letting bad habits take root leads to future misery. A parent who genuinely loves a child starts teaching and correcting him early in life. Loving correction keeps a child from growing up selfish and unruly.

A righteous person enjoys simple meals and has enough to feel fully satisfied, knowing God provides what is needed. The wicked may chase after endless pleasures and wealth, but their cravings are never satisfied and they remain empty inside. True contentment is a gift that money cannot buy.
